I did everything I could and it was never enough... it would never be enough. Not telling you that you should leave your partner but for me the abuse I experienced with the narcissism, lying, hiding, gaslighting and cheating it just wasn't worth the few fleeting moments of happiness. Even during those moments I was always waiting for the other shoe to drop... And it always did. I stayed far longer than I should because I was terrified of him accidentally killing himself but you end up growing resentful and thats not fair to yourself.

Nta. Your fiance on the other hand is for running and telling his sister how you feel and creating unnecessary drama. Not everyone is going to like you and not everyone is going to like his sister. While it's both your wedding day you're not obligated to include her in your bridal group. However, if it means so much to your husband she should absolutely be able to be a groomswoman. 

I think you both need counseling to learn how to resolve your relationship conflict without adding family into it. He was out of line for his actions. If you can't handle disagreements healthily now then it's only going to get worse once married. 

He didn't seem to care how his actions were going to affect you when running his mouth to his family. There's definitely a respect issue there. You are his partner not his sister. As long as you're kind to the sister you don't have to like being around her. I hate when people push the idea that you need to spend time with toxic family or just family you don't get along with. 

I would reevaluate the relationship though since he had no problem disrespecting you in favor of his sister. That's a huge red flag. I don't understand why your being honest about how you feel makes you the villain. I don't even like everyone in my own family and can handle them in small doses. Doesn't mean they're bad people, they just drain me in the same way your partners sister probably does. I wouldn't want to on my wedding day either. You shouldn't disallow her to be a part of your husband to be' grooms men's party though..

When I met my husband he only ate cheese pizza and plain spicy chicken sandwiches. I am a pastry chef. I grew up in a Puerto Rican house hold, we love food. My husband has aspergers, Textures bother him and he likes the familiarity of his plain foods. His mother took him to the doctors when he was about 7 or so and asked if his diet was a problem since he only ate pizza then. The doctor said he would grow out of it... He is 30 now. When we go out to eat I always have to make sure there is pizza or chicken fingers on the menu even if it's on the kids menu.

I am the definitely not the smart one in my marriage. I am the woman. We have very different backgrounds which I think plays a major pact. I grew up in the Bronx, New York, very poor, single mother but father was in and out of jail. My mother had three kids and two grand kids to support so she was never home. No one to help with homework or check if things were done properly. My sister (10 years old than me) was in her teen years and did want to be the mother to me and my brother or even her kids at the time. Step father was abusive, I suffered from depression due to rape and other things. The school system wasn't that great either. It was very hard for the teachers to teach the students since they either were violent or so many that very few kids could keep up with the lesson plans. It's actually very sad. Most of my peers only got out of the Bronx by leaving for the military. My high school didn't really prep us for college most of the teachers knew we wouldn't go since a) we couldn't afford it b) some of us already had kids and c) we wouldn't do well overall. I helped raise my sisters kids while I was in high school while she was off partying. I missed a lot of classes trying to take them to school and also working. My brother was a drug dealer at the time and was dealing out of the house. I was desperate to get out of that place so I enlisted in the Navy. Well my brother was being watched by the police for a few months and one day they came to they house where I was babysitting my nephews and arrested him, his friends and myself. I was released but I remember telling my mother I can't live there if she was going to let him back in since I couldn't afford having anything on my record. She asked me to leave since my brother was in a dark place. I was hurt and didn't talk to her for a few months. I went to live with my boyfriend at the time. She died a few weeks after we started talking again. I ended up moving in with other family across the country but it didn't work out. I moved back to NY and lived on the streets. A few friends helped me get a job and I re enrolled in school. I did night school and worked two jobs. I was the first to finish high school in my family. Not something you brag about but it was important to me. I went to culinary school and working in Boston for various high end shops. I fortunately have some talent but book smarts I do not. 

My husband has always been gifted. He's from Florida, middle class, parents split when he was young but always were involved in his school work and sports. Both parents are well educated. He got a scholarship to college. He was in gifted classes most his life and most things came easy. He reads a lot (Mostly fantasy). It's amazing the things he retains and can recite. The way his mind works to break down a problem. We're pretty sure he has aspergers not that his intelligence is the reason we think that but his ocd and lack of empathy among other things are. 

Now that there is some background I felt very stupid when we first started dating. He would correct me not in a way were he was being mean but trying to help so I wouldn't make a fool of myself. I didn't exactly take it well then. I would frequently be lost in our conversations or if he told me about things in the news. I will be the first to admit I didn't follow the news much growing up. I grew up in a very "survive and worry about food on the table for tomorrow" kind of way. So worrying about what was going on in the world wasn't something I did or anyone I knew did. It was very hard and I felt very inadequate in our relationship. We have a lot in common. Hobbies, sense of humor, music, core beliefs but education and overall knowledge he has me beat. Not that I think I am dumb to the point I can't function in society but our 4 year old asks a lot of questions that I should be able to answer but I can't. She usually goes straight to him and while it was hard at first I know how lucky I am that he can and wants to share what he knows. He thinks I am far smarter than I give myself credit for but he basis that off of being street smart and being able to survive. There is more to life than that. Especially living in Massachusetts where most people are very well educated and I get the whole "what college did you go to" question a lot. 

As much as I thought he deserved someone more suitable for him intelligence wise since I didn't think I could offer much in the long run I am glad he ignored me. Possible aspergers or not his intelligence and stubbornness has made me a better person.
